prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1297; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment grew to many times the usual amount for this injury, with near-daily visits and new body areas added weeks after the crash.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a sideswipe while changing lanes on a multi-lane road. The claimant's vehicle was reported as the other vehicle involved, and the claimant is represented by counsel, so all contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver involved is named on it and that coverage was active on the date of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Photos from the insured's phone show damage along the passenger side of the vehicle, and the pattern is consistent with the impact described. No independent witnesses have come forward so far.

Entry 4: Responding officer's report confirms the claimant was present in the other vehicle at the scene. Vehicle damage on the claimant's car matches the reported impact point, and no prior damage to that area is on record.

Entry 5: Recorded a first statement from the claimant through counsel. The account describes the same sequence of events given at the scene, and the claimant reported neck and back strain that is a plausible result of a collision of this kind.

Entry 6: Obtained the initial medical report. Treatment so far is limited and in line with what is typically expected for a neck and back strain. No prior injury to the same body areas is known.

Entry 7: Follow-up call with counsel to confirm the claimant's account has not changed. The description of the lane change and point of contact matches the earlier statement.

Entry 8: Treatment frequency has increased to nearly every day, and the claimant has been seen at a rate many times the usual for this injury. Additional body areas have been added in treatment notes several weeks after the crash.

Entry 9: Requested itemized treatment records and a provider summary to understand the increase in visits and the newly reported areas. Counsel has been informed the request is pending.

Entry 10: Reviewed the records received so far. The escalation in care is documented, but the provider notes give the reason for each added area, and no earlier injury to those areas appears in the prior records obtained.

Entry 11: Spoke again with the claimant through counsel. The account of how the collision happened remains the same as in every prior conversation. Further medical review has been requested before any evaluation is made.

Entry 12: File remains open pending the medical review and the remaining treatment records. Next step is to schedule the independent medical review and reassess the claim once that report is returned.
